llm.summary: The skill's code and instructions largely match its stated purpose, but the runtime instructions require running an external unpack script (not included) and rely on sending extracted document text to an AI for polishing, which are supply-chain and data-exfiltration risks you should review before use.

dimensions.detail: Name/description match the provided code: extract_comments.py parses comments.xml/document.xml and uses Word COM (pywin32) to obtain page numbers. Requiring Windows + Microsoft Word + pywin32 is coherent with the described page-number feature.

dimensions.detail: SKILL.md tells the user to run an external script at ~/.qoderwork/skills/docx/openxml/scripts/extract.py to unpack the .docx (not included in this package). That external step could execute arbitrary code or pull other tools. The skill also requires the agent to send extracted comment/anchor text to an AI for semantic polishing; SKILL.md does not constrain which endpoint is used, so sensitive document contents may be transmitted elsewhere.

dimensions.detail: No install spec is present and the code file is local. extract_comments.py is small, readable, and performs only XML parsing and optional Word COM calls — nothing downloaded or installed by the skill itself.

However, the core operation (AI-powered polishing) implies sending extracted text to an AI model or API — this is a data-sensitivity concern rather than a credential mismatch.

llm.guidance: This skill appears to implement comment extraction as described, but before you run it: 1) Inspect or avoid the external unpack script referenced (~/.qoderwork/…/extract.py) because it is not bundled here and could be arbitrary code; only run it if you trust its source. 2) Understand that the workflow expects you to use an AI to 'polish' comment text — that will send document contents to whatever model/endpoint the agent uses; do not use it on confidential documents unless you control/safeguard the AI endpoint (e.g., an on-prem model or approved enterprise API). 3) The script requires Windows + Microsoft Word + pywin32; Word will be automated via COM (it launches Word), so run in a controlled environment. 4) If you need higher assurance, open extract_comments.py locally and run it on sample data, and only use an AI endpoint you trust or keep polishing local.
